channelTitle: Why a turnip became a pumpkin - the end of Stingy Jack - Part 2
hook: In Part 1, Stingy Jack tricked the Devil twice and cheated death itself. Then Jack finally died - and that's when his real problem began.
storyParts: Years later Jack finally died of drink, and wandered to heaven's gate. But Saint Peter took one look at Jack's ledger of sins and shook his head - heaven doesn't take men who spent their lives swindling their neighbors.
So Jack trudged down to hell's door instead. But the Devil kept his promise and refused him too. As a parting insult, he tossed Jack a single burning coal from the inferno.

Jack hollowed out a turnip - his favorite vegetable - dropped the coal inside, and made himself a lantern. And there he stays: wandering the cold darkness between worlds, forever, with nowhere to rest.
The Irish called him Jack of the Lantern - Jack O'Lantern. They carved scary faces into turnips and set them in windows to frighten his wandering spirit away from their homes.

When Irish families emigrated to America, they discovered pumpkins - bigger, softer, brighter orange. And that's why every October, millions of porches still hold the face of a man too clever for heaven and too cursed for hell.
moral: Grandma June's takeaway: you can outsmart the Devil twice and still end up with nowhere to go - cleverness isn't the same as a life well lived.
cta: Do you carve pumpkins every year? Tell Grandma June your best design
